pages.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity visual HLD for one page of Adithya Rajendran's robotics/space portfolio. This is a buildable web design direction, not a diagram or device mockup. Wide 1536x1024 composition: show a desktop webpage header, hero, and the beginning of the next content section. Header: 'Adithya Rajendran' at left; 'Projects  Writing  Experience  About  Contact' at right. Manrope-like cream typography, dark ink background #101719, amber #DFA05D, sage #658761, restrained rust #AC5045. Large editorial headline on left, a carefully lit realistic THREE.JS-style mechanical scene across right 60%, integrated into a shared subtle Milky Way backdrop. Warm grazing sunlight, cool edge fill, dark crevices, believable metal and ceramic surfaces, restrained emissive amber/cyan instrument lights. Seamless fade into the page, no visible boxed image. Clear readable text, generous space. No HUD clutter, no invented career achievements, no dashboard. The supporting artwork is imaginative future-space engineering. Page: PROJECTS. Headline exactly 'Ideas, made real.' Eyebrow 'SELECTED WORK / PROJECTS'. Supporting copy 'Experiments in perception, memory, and reliable systems.' Link 'Explore the projects ↓'. Hero: sophisticated orbital research workshop above a broad cratered lunar limb, viewed three-quarter with perspective. Central cylindrical docking hub, habitat ring with segmented pressure vessels and a dozen warm windows, connected structural trusses, long dark indigo solar arrays, radiators, docking collars, two small maintenance craft. Mechanical detail and physically plausible connections; stronger depth and size variation than a generic floating satellite. Moon is a large partial backdrop fading into shadow, not a small sphere behind the model. Bottom shows 'Selected projects' and beginnings of clean project research cards with real charts, not fake space projects. A discreet line below art reads '01 / BUILD · The orbital workshop' and 'Pause motion'.

pages.name: detail-layouts
pages.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity HLD design board with TWO complete, distinct desktop content-page compositions side-by-side, each titled outside its page: 'Project detail' and 'Article'. Adithya Rajendran robotics/space portfolio. Theme #101719 charcoal, cream typography, #DFA05D amber, sage #658761, shared subtle star sky at the top, clean Manrope type. Each mini-page has the same navigation: Projects, Writing, Experience, About, Contact. Match a refined realistic space-themed portfolio but these are calm readable content pages, NOT dashboards. LEFT project detail: breadcrumb '← Projects', large title 'Evaluating detectors on driving scenes', short summary, a subtle orbital line and small section marker, a broad honest scientific comparison plot with amber error bars on cream paper, structured 'Overview' and 'Results' content sections below, small technology tags. RIGHT article: breadcrumb '← Writing', large title 'A Homelab Built to Be Rebuilt', date/byline, restrained Contents navigation, a quiet horizontal abstract star-trajectory strip that fades to paper-like dark reading surface, readable paragraphs and clear subheads. Light depth and excellent spacing. No WebGL scenes filling reading space, no invented results, no stock photos, no sidebar navigation, no glows around all cards. Show enough hierarchy to implement the entire reading flow. Approx 2048x1536.

Shared header on each 'Adithya Rajendran' and Projects, Writing, Experience, About, Contact. LEFT: quiet topic archive with eyebrow 'WRITING / TOPIC', title 'Robotics', subtitle 'Notes and experiments in perception and autonomy.', clean article rows with dates and clear warm links, thin trajectory line visually connecting archive entries. Avoid huge space art on archive page. RIGHT: elegant error page with small '404 / AN UNEXPECTED TURN', headline 'Page not found.', a restrained spherical orbital graphic of thin warm elliptical tracks with one tiny signal/craft drifting outside the orbit, no giant arbitrary digits, and clear 'Return home ↗' / 'Explore projects ↗' actions.
